Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant journey you've been on, becoming a new mother, and I'm honored to be a part of your postpartum care. Today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a screening tool designed to help us understand your emotional well-being during this important time. The EPDS screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it's a valuable tool in helping us provide the best possible support for you.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings. This assessment is not about judging or diagnosing; it's about understanding your experiences and ensuring you receive the care and support you need.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us better understand your emotional state over the past 7 days. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings as openly as you're comfortable. Remember, there are no right or wrong answers; this is about your personal experience.

Let's get started. I want to begin by asking: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

(sighing slightly) Honestly, it's been a bit of a struggle to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I still enjoy watching my baby laugh and play, and that brings me some joy. But overall, I just don't feel like myself. I used to be able to laugh and joke around with my friends and family, but now it feels like it takes a lot more effort to find things funny. Some days are better than others, but most of the time, I just feel... tired and overwhelmed. (pausing, looking down) I do still get some pleasure from a few things, like reading to my baby or taking a warm bath, but it's just not the same as it was before. (looking up, slightly tearfully) I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a new mom, instead of really enjoying it like I thought I would.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(shaking my head) No, not really. Like I said, it's been a struggle to find the humor in things. I feel like I'm just trying to get through each day, and laughing doesn't come as easily as it used to. (pausing, looking down) I don't feel like myself, and it's hard to explain. I just feel... sad and overwhelmed a lot of the time. (sighing) Even when my baby does something cute or funny, I might smile, but it's not the same as really laughing and feeling carefree like I used to. (looking up, with a hint of tears in my eyes) Does that make sense.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking my head slightly) Not as much as I used to. I mean, I'll make plans to do things, like go for a walk or meet a friend, but when the time comes, I just don't feel like doing it. (sighing) I've been having trouble sleeping, and when I do finally get some rest, I wake up feeling anxious and overwhelmed. It's hard to enjoy things when I'm feeling so tired and worried all the time. (pausing, looking down) Sometimes I'll think about doing something I used to love, like reading a book or watching a movie, but it just doesn't sound as appealing as it used to. (looking up) I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a new mom, instead of really enjoying the experience. (my voice cracks slightly) It's hard to explain, but I just feel like I've lost my sense of purpose and enjoyment in things.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding, looking down) Yes... I do that a lot. As a new mom, I feel like I'm supposed to have all the answers and be perfect all the time. When things don't go as planned, or if my baby cries and I don't know how to soothe her, I feel like it's all my fault. (sighing) I'll think to myself, "If only I had done this differently, or if only I had known that..." It's like I'm constantly criticizing myself and wondering what I could have done better. (looking up, with a hint of tears) Even when my partner or family members try to reassure me that I'm doing a great job, I still can't shake the feeling that I'm somehow failing as a mother. (my voice barely above a whisper) It's like I'm waiting for someone to tell me that I'm not good enough, and that I'm just pretending to be a mom.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Oh, yes... all the time. I worry about everything. Is my baby eating enough? Is she sleeping too much or too little? Is she developing normally? (my voice starts to tremble) I'll be sitting there, feeding her or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll think, "What if something's wrong with her? What if I'm missing some sign or symptom?" (taking a deep breath) And then I'll start to worry about all the things that could go wrong, like SIDS or accidents or illnesses... (shaking my head) It's like my mind is constantly racing with worst-case scenarios. (looking down, my voice barely above a whisper) Sometimes I'll be awake in the middle of the night, just lying there, thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and I'll feel this overwhelming sense of anxiety and fear. (pausing, looking up) It's like I'm waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? Like, something's going to go terribly wrong, and it's all going to be my fault.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, taking a deep breath) Yes... that's happened to me too. Sometimes I'll be sitting there, just feeding my baby or playing with her, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. (shaking my head) It's so irrational, because everything is fine, but my mind just starts to spiral out of control. (looking down, my voice barely above a whisper) I'll think to myself, "What if I'm not good enough? What if I'm failing as a mother?" And then the thoughts just start to snowball, and I'll feel like I'm losing control. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sometimes I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll feel this crushing sense of anxiety, like something's going to happen, but I don't know what. (looking up, tears in my eyes) It's like I'm living in a constant state of hypervigilance, just waiting for something to go wrong. (my voice cracks) And it's exhausting, because I'm always on edge, always waiting for the other shoe to drop.
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding, feeling a lump form in my throat) Yes... that's exactly how I feel. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to be a good partner and friend... it all just feels so overwhelming. (sighing) Some days, I feel like I'm just barely holding it together. I'll be okay for a little while, and then something will happen, like the baby will cry and I won't know how to soothe her, or I'll spill something on the floor, and it'll just feel like the last straw. (looking down, my voice shaking) I'll think to myself, "I just can't do this anymore. I'm not cut out for this mom thing." (pausing, taking a deep breath) And then I'll feel guilty for feeling that way, because I know I'm supposed to be grateful for my baby and my life. But it's just hard, you know? It feels like everything is getting on top of me, and I don't know how to climb out from under it all. (tears start to fall, and I look up, feeling a sense of desperation) I just wish someone could help me, you know? I wish someone could just take some of this weight off my shoulders and tell me that everything is going to be okay.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, feeling a sense of relief that someone is finally asking about my sleep) Oh, yes... sleep has been a real struggle for me. I'll lie awake at night, just thinking about everything that's going on, and I'll feel this overwhelming sense of sadness and anxiety. (sighing) It's like my mind is racing, and I just can't turn it off. I'll think about all the things I need to do, and all the things that could go wrong, and it just keeps me up. (looking down, my voice barely above a whisper) Sometimes I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll just feel this crushing sense of despair. I'll think to myself, "I'll never be a good mom. I'll never be able to do this." (pausing, taking a deep breath) And then I'll feel guilty for feeling that way, because I know I'm supposed to be happy and grateful for my baby. But it's just hard, you know? It feels like everything is just weighing on me, and I don't know how to shake it off. (looking up, tears in my eyes) I've been having trouble falling asleep, and when I do finally drift off, I'll wake up a few hours later, feeling anxious and overwhelmed. It's like I'm just not getting any rest, and it's making everything feel even harder. (my voice cracks) I just wish I could sleep, you know? I just wish I could feel rested and refreshed, and not feel like I'm just barely holding on.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, feeling a lump form in my throat) Yes... I've been feeling really sad and miserable a lot lately. It's like this constant cloud is following me around, and I just can't shake it off. (sighing) I'll be doing okay, and then something will remind me of my old life, or I'll think about how I'm not the same person I used to be, and it'll just hit me. (looking down, my voice barely above a whisper) I'll feel this wave of sadness wash over me, and it's like I'm drowning in it. I'll think to myself, "I'll never be happy again. I'll never be me again." (pausing, taking a deep breath) And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, I'll be feeding my baby, and I'll just start crying because I'm so overwhelmed. Or I'll be trying to get her to sleep, and I'll just feel so frustrated and sad because it's not working. (looking up, tears in my eyes) It's like I'm just feeling everything so intensely, and it's hard to cope with. (my voice cracks) Sometimes I'll just break down and cry, and I won't even know why. It's like my emotions are just too much for me to handle. (wiping away tears) I just feel so sad and lost, and I don't know how to find my way back to being happy again.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears welling up in my eyes) Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like I'm just so overwhelmed and sad, and I don't know how to process it all. (sighing) I'll be doing okay, and then something will trigger me, and I'll just start crying. It could be something as simple as a commercial on TV, or a song that reminds me of my old life. (looking down, my voice barely above a whisper) Sometimes I'll be holding my baby, and I'll just start crying because I'm so overwhelmed with love and gratitude, but also with fear and anxiety. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's like my emotions are just so raw and close to the surface, and it doesn't take much to set me off. (looking up, tears streaming down my face) I've been crying a lot at night, when my baby is sleeping, and my partner is trying to comfort me. I've been crying in the shower, or while I'm driving in the car. (my voice cracks) It's like I'm just so unhappy, and I don't know how to make it stop. (sobbing) I just feel so lost and alone, and I don't know how to find my way back to being happy again. (wiping away tears) I'm sorry, I'm just really struggling right now.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(looking down, my voice barely above a whisper) Yes... I've had those thoughts. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's like, when everything feels too much, and I'm just so overwhelmed, my mind will start to wander to dark places. (looking up, tears in my eyes) I'll think to myself, "What if I just didn't exist anymore? What if I just disappeared?" (my voice cracks) It's not that I really want to hurt myself, it's just that sometimes it feels like the only way to escape the pain and the sadness. (shaking my head) But then I think about my baby, and my partner, and my family, and I know that I could never do that to them. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I've had those thoughts, but I don't think I would ever act on them. (looking down, my voice barely above a whisper) I just wish I could find a way to make the pain stop, you know? I wish I could find a way to be happy again, and to feel like myself again. (tears streaming down my face) I'm just so tired of feeling this way, and I don't know how to make it stop.

The patient is experiencing a range of emotional difficulties following the birth of their baby, including persistent feelings of sadness, anxiety, and overwhelm. They report struggling to find pleasure in activities, feeling guilty and self-critical, and having difficulty coping with their emotions and responsibilities as a new mother. The patient's responses suggest a strong need for support and understanding, and a comprehensive assessment is necessary to determine the best course of action.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 28, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>the 'Not at all' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a significant decrease in looking forward to things with enjoyment, using phrases such as 'Not as much as I used to' and 'it just doesn't sound as appealing as it used to', which aligns with the option 'Definitely less than I used to'.</sym>, <sym>The patient admits to frequently blaming themselves when things go wrong, and this pattern of thought is persistent, even when reassured by others, indicating a strong tendency towards self-criticism.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, very often' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates frequent and intense feelings of panic and anxiety, even in situations where there is no apparent reason to feel scared or panicky, such as when feeding or playing with her baby.</sym>, <sym>the guideline option 'Yes, most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all</sym>, <sym>The patient describes having significant difficulty sleeping due to overwhelming sadness, anxiety, and despair, indicating that they have been unhappy most of the time, which aligns with the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates feeling sad and miserable most of the time, with intense emotions and frequent breakdowns, matching the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient admits to having thoughts of self-harm, but states they don't think they would ever act on them, indicating these thoughts occur sometimes, aligning with the 'Sometimes' option.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's symptoms and concerns are consistent with the <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. The EPDS score of 28 indicates a high risk for <med>postpartum depression</med>, and the patient's report of suicidal thoughts requires immediate attention and further assessment. The patient's emotional difficulties, including <sym>sadness</sym>, <sym>anxiety</sym>, and <sym>guilt</sym>, are consistent with the diagnostic criteria for <med>postpartum depression</med>. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med>
2. Refer to <med>mental health specialist</med> for further evaluation and treatment
3. Encourage patient to reach out to support groups or online resources for <med>postpartum depression</med>
4. Develop a safety plan to address suicidal thoughts and ensure patient's safety
5. Provide patient with resources for emergency crisis services, such as the <med>National Suicide Prevention Lifeline</med>
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
